components.gap: Reconstruct Fisher 1922's complete estimation/information/sufficiency presentation so that each estimate and theorem has explicit model, sampling and regularity scope. Still missing: (1) Type II form parameters: condition (C) of def:p15-w02b-p15-057-multi-conditions is not verified, so the inverse-information values of thm:p15-w02b-p15-057-form-ii are not shown to be the limit variances of any root of the likelihood equations (body 1438-1443); (2) the efficiency contours of Fisher's figs. 3-4 on the Types I/II side of the normal point (y>0) are not shown to be the efficiencies of those curves (body 1129-1132); (3) Fisher's conclusion that the moments have at least 80 per cent form-efficiency for symmetric Pearson curves exactly when beta_2 lies between 2.65 and 3.42 requires monotonicity of E_r on each side, which the text states is not proved (body 1434-1438); (4) the numerical claims E_r=0.8 at r=17.172 (beta_2=3.4234), E_nu=0.8 at r=12.112, the Type II crossings r=14.059 and r=10.985, E_nu>E_r at every tabulated r, the Type VII and Type II table reproductions and the r=10 value 0.4289 against the printed 0.4403 are asserted in body prose (1340-1353, 1423-1433) with no written computation or certified bound in the annex; (5) the large-r expansions in item 3 of thm:p15-w02b-p15-057-form-ii are asserted to 'follow as in the Type VII proof' (annex 2231-2236), and in the form-vii proof the simplification of the efficiency factors and the expansion G_r=6-4r^{-2}+12r^{-3}+O(r^{-4}) of the rational part are stated without written steps (annex 2088-2102); (6) Fisher's p. 337 statement that the weight of the end-point location determination grows faster than n at p=1 whether or not a and p are known is proved only with a and the shape known (body 1603-1606); (7) Fisher's grouped-normal efficiency comparison (pp. 361-363): the further losses from using the grouped mean and the Sheppard-corrected second moment instead of the grouped maximum likelihood estimate are given only as information-benchmark comparisons, without a theorem giving those estimators' limit variances under the stated grouped sampling (host fisher-grouping 326-334 says a delta-method/regular-estimator theorem would be required); the claim that the grouping loss stays below 1 per cent for an interval below sigma/4 is neither certified nor corrected; and Fisher's p. 363 remark that moderate grouping discards most of the information for curves meeting the axis at a finite angle or with a finite or infinite end ordinate is not treated; (8) Fisher's Section 5 fourfold-table example (p. 317: the correlation of a dichotomized normal surface determined uniquely by the criterion of consistency) is not treated anywhere on the route; (9) Fisher's large-sample error of the median for the Cauchy location curve (p. 322) and its comparison with maximum likelihood (variance 2/n in thm:p15-w02b-p15-057-cauchy-check) are not reconstructed (host fisher-estimation 320-321 disclaims it).
